newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Six NZ work stoppages ended in June - SNZ.
newsitem.headline: Six NZ work stoppages ended in June - SNZ.

text.p: Six New Zealand work stoppages ended in June, 1996, Statistics New Zealand said on Wednesday.
Five were complete strikes and one was a complete lockout.
"Together, these involved 4,817 employees and resulted in the loss of 13,477 person-days of work and about NZ$1.723 million in wages and salaries," SNZ said.
It said 17 stoppages ended in the June 1996 quarter involving 9,259 employees. There were 17,979 person-days of work and an estimated $2.4 million in wages and salaries lost.
SNZ said there were 67 stoppages in the year to June 30, 1996, involving 15,030 employees, which was fewer than the 32,750 in the year to June 1995 and the 17,774 in the year to June 1994.

Stoppages that ended in the 12 months to June 30 1996 resulted in the loss of 29,799 person-days of work. This was fewer than the 53,286 days lost in the year to June 1995 and the 39,634 lost in the year to June 1994.
"An estimated $3.9 million in wages and salaries was lost in the June 1996 year, compared with $6.8 million in the June 1995 year and $4.7 million in the June 1994 year," SNZ said.
It said 35 of the 67 stoppages in the year to June 1996 occurred in the private sector, with the remaining 32 in the public sector.
As well as the six stoppages ending in June 1996, 10 other stoppages were still in progress.
